## When you'd use this

The builder's **Layout** blocks put words on the form without asking anything: they introduce a section, explain what comes next, or break a long form into parts. The example above has one of each.

<UseCases>
<UseCase title="Heading">
A heading for a section, at level 1, 2 or 3, such as "About your visit".
</UseCase>
<UseCase title="Text">
A paragraph of plain text, such as how long the form takes or who sees the answers. Line breaks you type are kept.
</UseCase>
<UseCase title="Divider">
A horizontal rule between two parts of the form.
</UseCase>
<UseCase title="Title">
A larger heading, always at level 2, such as "Contact details".
</UseCase>
<UseCase title="Label">
A short line of text in a quieter colour, such as a note about which questions are required.
</UseCase>
</UseCases>

To group questions under a heading that is part of the group, use a group instead: its label is its heading.

## Before you start

- You need a form open in the editor.
- These blocks collect no answer. They have no **Required** and no **Help text**, aren't numbered, and can't be used as the source of a condition.
- Each one can have conditions of its own, under **Logic**, so it shows only when they pass.

## Steps

### Add a heading

1. Below the last block, select **+** (Insert a block), or type `/` in the line beside it.
2. Under **Layout**, choose **Heading 1**, **Heading 2** or **Heading 3**.
3. In **Label**, write the heading. The label is the heading respondents see.
4. To change its level later, choose **H1**, **H2** or **H3** under **Level**.

### Add text

1. Insert a block, and under **Layout**, choose **Text**. Typing `paragraph` finds it too.
2. In **Content**, replace "Add some descriptive text here." with your text. Respondents see the content, never the **Label**.

### Add a divider

1. Insert a block, and under **Layout**, choose **Divider**. Typing `line` or `separator` finds it too.
2. Keep or change its **Label**. Respondents don't see it, but screen readers announce it as the divider's name.

### Add a title

1. Insert a block, and under **Layout**, choose **Title**.
2. In **Content**, replace "Section title" with your title. Respondents see the content; if it is empty, they see the **Label** instead.

### Add a label

1. Insert a block, and under **Layout**, choose **Label**.
2. In **Content**, replace "Label" with your text. Respondents see the content; if it is empty, they see the **Label** instead.

Then select **Save**.

<Note>
For Heading, Divider, Title and Label, the settings are headed **Question**, and the Logic section reads **Show this question only when…**. They still collect no answer.
</Note>

## What happens behind the scenes

- **Heading** is a heading element at its level: Heading 1 is `h1`, Heading 2 `h2`, Heading 3 `h3`.
- **Title** is always an `h2`, drawn larger than a Heading 2.
- **The form's own title isn't shown as a heading** by the renderer: the page the form sits in has its own. A group's label is a level 2 heading, or level 3 in a form with pages, under the page title, so a Heading 2 sits at the same level as a group.
- **Text** is a paragraph. It is plain text, never HTML or Markdown, so `*` or `<b>` show as typed. A Text block with no content, or only spaces, shows nothing.
- **Divider** is a horizontal rule (`<hr>`) named by its Label.
- **Label** is a line of plain text, in the form's muted colour.
- **Nothing from these blocks is sent** with the answers.
- **A group or page that shows nothing is hidden.** If every block in a group or page is hidden by conditions, or shows nothing, such as an empty Text block, the group's heading isn't shown either, and in a form with pages the page is skipped.

## Rules the builder enforces

| What you try | What the builder says |
|---|---|
| Save a Text block with no content | Text block "About you › Text" is empty — add some text or delete it. (under the Content field: This text block is empty — add some text or delete it.) |

The name in quotation marks is the block's path: the page and groups it is in, then its label.

## Troubleshooting

**Respondents don't see what you typed in Label.** For Text, Title and Label blocks, respondents see **Content**. A Text block's Label is never shown to them; a Title's or Label's is shown only when its Content is empty.

**Text shows `*` or `<b>` instead of formatting.** Text is plain text. Use Heading, Title or Label blocks for emphasis.

**A section heading disappeared.** Every block in the group is hidden by its conditions, or shows nothing, so the whole group is hidden.
